nodes.title: The YT playlist lane repaired - three independent faults, none of them the rate limit
nodes.description: Gavin: 'when i say YT is broken this is what i mean - fix the /cinopsis:cinopsis code for the YT playlist side with the fixes we just discussed instead of duct taping it, use /prism:griot-agent-architect.' Run as an ICM stage-walk: a contract at .prism/shared/plans/yt-ladder-fix-CONTEXT.md carrying the verified findings and locked decisions, handed to a headless claude -p in the repo with a thin router prompt. The agent implemented, hit an execution boundary, and handed back DGS_SYNC_INCOMPLETE rather than claiming done; this session finished steps 7-9 and found two bugs only running it could surface.

verification.evidence: Cinopsis commit 18a9868, pushed, local HEAD == origin/main. 'claude plugin validate .' -> Validation passed. Live pull, no env vars set: HDGJJA__9FQ 354 segments, RTmTebnxwKc 277, oUHpTApgbhQ 512 - all via selenium-panel on the attached Profile 1 session.
verification.result: built-and-live - the lane pulls transcripts out of the box for the first time in weeks.

nodes.title: Three independent faults each presented as the same symptom - 'all rungs failed'
nodes.description: The YT lane's failure looked like one problem and was three. F1: the cdp-panel rung was OPT-IN and nothing ever set CINOPSIS_ENABLE_CDP, so the rung built specifically to survive an IP flag had never run. F2: selenium was not installed, so selenium-panel had never run either. F3: both panel rungs defaulted to HEADLESS, and YouTube does not render the transcript panel to a headless session. Any one of these produces the identical ladder output - 'all rungs failed' - which is indistinguishable from a rate-limit block. That is why weeks of playlist trouble kept getting attributed to hammering YouTube when the gate was in fact working perfectly the whole time.

verification.evidence: F1: '[cdp] CINOPSIS_ENABLE_CDP not set; skipping CDP rung (opt-in only)'. F2: '[selenium-panel] driver unavailable: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named selenium'. F3: same video, same scraper, same minute - PT.fetch_segments('fzobKIjUN_E', headed=True) returned 237 segments, headed=False returned 0.
verification.result: defect-fixed - cdp on by default, selenium pinned in requirements.txt at >=4.49.0, headed made structural rather than a flag.

nodes.title: ONE ORIGINAL - the session problem was solved once and then forked
nodes.description: grab_transcript_cdp.py had already solved YouTube session acquisition by importing the signed-in PROFILE_DIR from export_yt_cookies. panel_transcript.py independently re-solved the same problem badly, building its driver on tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='ytpanel_') - signed out, no cookies, no Premium. Gavin named the principle directly: 'this is exactly what i meant when i said ONE ORIGINAL.' Two implementations of one idea, and the worse one silently won because it was the rung being called.

verification.evidence: scripts/chrome_session.py now exposes acquire_session() as the single seam; both panel rungs call it and nothing else. Its docstring records the rejected alternatives: a profile copy (WAL-journaled SQLite plus App-Bound Encryption), cookie-jar injection (the fork itself), and asking Gavin to close Chrome (named as duct tape in the contract).
verification.result: defect-fixed - one seam, consumed by both rungs, with the losing options written down rather than silently dropped.

nodes.title: Chrome's singleton lock made the right profile unusable until the port was opened at launch
nodes.description: Chrome enforces one process per --user-data-dir, and cannot enable remote debugging on an already-running process. Gavin's Chrome GB is normally open on Profile 1, so pointing Selenium at that directory crashed - observed as chromedriver's GetHandleVerifier stack, exit 1 - exactly when the panel rungs matter most. Telling him to close his browser to run a batch was explicitly ruled out as duct tape.

verification.evidence: scripts/launch_chrome_debug.ps1 probes 127.0.0.1:9333 first and only launches if nothing is listening. After running it: port 9333 returns Chrome/152.0.7977.83, and a real pull logs '[chrome-session] attached to existing Chrome on Profile 1 (port 9333)'.
verification.result: defect-fixed - one-time launch with the port open, every run afterwards attaches. Standing cost: a normal Chrome restart closes the port until relaunched through the script.

nodes.title: Two bugs that reasoning could not have caught, and an agent that refused to claim done
nodes.description: The headless architect run implemented everything and then hit a permission wall on Bash/python. It ran the Stuck Protocol across three surfaces, reported DGS_SYNC_INCOMPLETE, and explicitly declined to print DONE_YT_LADDER_FIX. Finishing the verification by hand found two defects no amount of reading could have surfaced. First, grab_transcript_cdp.py lost 'import json' during the refactor while still calling json in four places - NameError on every cdp attempt. Second, selenium-panel had been left opt-in on the stated reasoning that it is 'a redundant, slower backup behind cdp-panel driving the identical session'; on the SAME attached session cdp-panel reports 'transcript panel never populated' while selenium-panel returns 487 entries, so the reasoning was exactly inverted.

verification.evidence: Live ladder output: '[ladder] trying rung: cdp-panel' -> '[cdp] transcript panel never populated' -> '[ladder] trying rung: selenium-panel' -> '[ladder] selenium-panel succeeded (487 entries)' on OQipTxv9Qv0.
verification.result: corrected-verified - selenium-panel flipped ON by default with the correction written into the code at the decision point, not into a changelog. The honest incomplete is what made the fix real; a green checkmark would have shipped two live bugs.
